Sophie — thanks for the clear note and the redline. Looping in Kimberly from Legal to work the language; will include Laura from Sales Ops if we need to model billing implications. Quick thoughts below: 

- Auto-renew: Redwood is comfortable with an explicit opt-out window. We typically do 30 days before renewal + automated reminder at 45 days; happy to codify that in the Order Form and confirm notification mechanics (email to procurement + account owner).

- Termination for convenience: our standard approach is to allow termination for convenience for Order Forms but with a limited wind-down fee to cover reserved capacity commitments on Dedicated pools. Options we can propose:
  • Option A: 45-day notice, no early termination fee if customer reduces committed capacity proactively and provides 30-day migration window.
  • Option B: 60-day notice with a pro-rated unwind fee equal to 25% of remaining committed monthly fees for up to 3 months.
  • Option C: Mutual termination for convenience (both parties) with a one-time transition credit equal to one month of committed capacity, plus data export assistance (S3 export + 2 runbook hours).

I'll summarize and attach a short RFC (RDF-summary-ben-20270503.pdf) for legal to review. If Kimberly can indicate which of the options is closest to acceptable, I'll pull together a clean Order Form edit and plan the DocuSign timeline.

Next steps: Kimberly — any immediate do-not-accept flags? Sophie — which option would you prefer us to draft into the doc?

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference

Ben / team —

Thanks for the context. Reviewed Sophie’s redline and Ben’s proposed options. High level position from Legal: we can accept mutual termination for convenience on the Order Form, but we need to protect Redwood's exposure for Reserved/Dedicated capacity. Proposed redlines (high level):

- Notice window: set at 45 days for Order Form termination for convenience. Rationale: balances customer flexibility with our capacity reallocation window.

- Auto-renew: accept a 12-month renewal term with a 30-day opt-out prior to renewal; require Redwood to send an automated renewal reminder at 45 days and a final notice at 30 days. Add explicit language on what constitutes effective notice (email to procurement email on file + portal acknowledgment).

- Early termination fees / wind-down: cap fees to the lesser of (i) 3 months of committed fees or (ii) remaining pre-paid balance. Alternatively, offer a transition credit equal to one month of committed capacity when Customer elects mutual termination and Redwood takes a defined migration-assistance step. Include a definition of "migration assistance" (data export in standard format within 7 days of request + up to 8 hours of engineer time for runbook/transfer support).

- Dedicated capacity carve-out: explicit clause that if Dedicated capacity is deprovisioned on Customer request, Redwood will provide a three-month notice to third-party infra partners where relevant and make commercially reasonable efforts to reassign capacity; any charges owed under third-party contracts will be passed through if incurred before termination effective date.

- SOW vs MSA: move detailed operational SLA and handover obligations into the SOW, but keep notice/fee mechanics in Order Form.

I'll prepare a redline to the Order Form reflecting the 45-day notice + capped fee OR the one-month transition credit alternative. Ben — if you want to lean into Option C (transition credit + data export), say so and I'll draft accordingly.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Agreed commercial guardrails (to be reflected in the Order Form):
- Renewal: 12-month term, 30-day opt-out prior to renewal; Redwood to send automated reminders at 45 and 30 days to procurement@sproutpay.com and account owner.
- Termination for convenience: Mutual termination for convenience is acceptable for the Order Form with a 45-day notice window.

- Migration assistance: Redwood will provide standard data export (S3-compatible export within 7 days) + up to 8 hours of engineering runbook/time. Detailed operational SLAs and steps will be moved to the SOW.
